**1. `deleteComment` does not check who wrote the comment.**
- The handler takes only `@Param() params` and passes `(slug, id)` to the service (`src/article/article.controller.ts:85-87`). It never reads the caller with `@User(...)`.
- The service signature is `deleteComment(slug, id)` and has no user argument (`src/article/article.service.ts:114`). Its only check is that the comment is in this article's `comments` list (`article.service.ts:118`). It then deletes it (`article.service.ts:121-122`).
- The `Comment` entity has only `id`, `body` and `article` (`src/article/comment.entity.ts:7-14`). It has no author column, so there is nothing to compare against.
- The route does need a valid token, because `articles/:slug/comments/:id` with DELETE is in the middleware list (`src/article/article.module.ts:29`). The middleware only sets `req.user` (`src/user/auth.middleware.ts:24`). So any logged-in user can delete any comment.
- The `403 Forbidden` Swagger line on this handler (`article.controller.ts:83`) describes a check that doesn't exist.

**2. Profile routes with the auth middleware**

| Route | Handler | Middleware? |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /profiles/:username` | `profile.controller.ts:18` | No |
| `POST /profiles/:username/follow` | `profile.controller.ts:23` | Yes |
| `DELETE /profiles/:username/follow` | `profile.controller.ts:28` | Yes |

The module applies `AuthMiddleware` to `profiles/:username/follow` with `RequestMethod.ALL` (`src/profile/profile.module.ts:20-22`). That covers both follow and unfollow. `GET /profiles/:username` is public. It calls `@User('id')` (`profile.controller.ts:19`), but that decorator only reads an identity if a token is sent and doesn't block anyone. I took that behaviour from `.claude/knowledge/auth.md:28-35` and did not open `user.decorator.ts`.

**3. The `RO` suffix means "Response Object".**
- It marks the interface that wraps what a handler returns, e.g. `ArticleRO` is `{ article }` (`src/article/article.interface.ts:24`).
- The others are `ArticlesRO` (`article.interface.ts:28`), `CommentsRO` (`article.interface.ts:20`), `UserRO` (`src/user/user.interface.ts:9`) and `ProfileRO` (`src/profile/profile.interface.ts:8`).
- The source files never spell out "Response Object". That expansion comes from `.claude/knowledge/workspace.md:62`.

I did not read `profile.service.ts`, `app.module.ts`, `user.module.ts` or `user.decorator.ts`. A global middleware set up in `app.module.ts` would change the profile answer, but `auth.md` says the three module `configure()` blocks are the only place it's applied.
